review_comments.body:
This test takes ~9s. `backend/azure` can't set `azblobclient.retryOptions`, so every subtest goes through the SDK default retries (3 retries, 0.8s/1.6s/3.2s backoff). Override retries per call:

```go
ctx := policy.WithRetryOptions(context.Background(), policy.RetryOptions{MaxRetries: -1})
```

(import `github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-go/sdk/azcore/policy`). It runs in ~0.7s with that.

`ClientOptions()` now runs on every request, and its result depends on a mutable package global that only exists for tests. Since `policy.WithRetryOptions(ctx, ...)` overrides retries per call, please drop `retryOptions`: switch `TestNewKeepsSASOutOfTransportErrors` to the context override and remove `Retry` here. That keeps the exported function pure, avoids a latent data race if a test ever runs in parallel, and removes the duplicated "zero value / tests" note in both doc comments.
Nit: the added sentence documents caller obligations of another package on an unexported type, and repeats the `ClientOptions` doc. Please keep the original comment.
Nit: this comment is on only one of the three helpers. Drop it or make it consistent (moot if the clients are derived from the service client).

Same leak through a different path, not covered by this policy (pre-existing): if the SAS token contains a control character, e.g. a trailing `\n` from a Kubernetes secret in `AZ_SAS_TOKEN`, `http.NewRequestWithContext` fails before the pipeline runs and every request logs:

`parse "http://…/acct/testbucket?restype=container&sv=…&sig=SECRET\n": net/url: invalid control character in URL`

Reproduced on both the service client and the per-container client. Validate the token once in `New` (e.g. `url.ParseQuery`, rejecting control characters) with an error that doesn't echo the token.

"every blob client must use" isn't true in the tree: `copySourceURL` still builds `service.NewClient(az.serviceURL, az.defaultCreds, nil)` (`backend/azure/copy.go:66`). It can't leak a SAS (no query there), but either use `az.client.ServiceClient()` there (same credentials) or soften the wording.

This is optional, because it's a pre-existing bug. I'm ok with fixing it in a follow up PR or just report the issue in backlog.

A token copied with a leading `?` (`?sv=...&sig=...`) fails on `main` and on this branch alike (AuthorizationFailure on every call against Azurite). With the derived clients, `runtime.JoinPaths` splits the endpoint on `?`, so per-blob requests now go out with no SAS at all instead of a garbled one. Since `New` validates the token now, consider `sasToken = strings.TrimPrefix(sasToken, "?")` here, or rejecting it with a hint.

comments.body: This won't automatically run in continuous integration without approval. A member of the Versity organization must allow it.

Applied the requested service-client derivation and per-call retry overrides, removed ClientOptions and retryOptions, and restored the original policy comment. `copySourceURL` is unchanged: the "every blob client" wording went away with ClientOptions, and that client carries no SAS. Added initialization validation for malformed SAS queries with a token-free error and regression tests. The backend/azure and internal/azblobclient suites and go vet pass.


This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Applied the latest review: the invalid-token subtests are now named cases, the two rejections say why without echoing the token ("contains a control character" / "malformed query") using `strings.ContainsFunc`, and a leading `?` on the SAS token is trimmed in `New` (with a test). `go test ./internal/azblobclient ./backend/azure` passes.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
